trust_decision.summary: File::sanitizePath() decides whether a caller-supplied directory value is safe to use as a path relative to the filesystem disk root; at the pinned commit it whitelists '.' and '/', so '..' segments survive and the caller's directory can escape the disk root.

landing_point.why: The advisory names File::sanitizePath() and the fix's only source hunk rewrites that one method (fix.diff:33-43).

fix_sites.module_kind: helper library class shared by the uploader, the mover and the image-manipulation builder

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/MediaUploader.php:739-746 (import() assigns the raw $directory to $model->directory at :746, never calling sanitizePath; reached from importPath() at src/MediaUploader.php:715-722 and from media:import at src/Commands/ImportMediaCommand.php:128)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: import() only registers a file that is already on the disk and never writes anything, so a solver can argue the write-side directory-traversal protection does not cover it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Directory segments that legitimately contain dots ('2024.10', 'v1.0', or a last segment like 'bar.jpg') are rewritten to '-' by the new per-segment regex (fix.diff:41), and the stored directory is pushed back through sanitizePath on rename and replace: Media::rename() passes $this->directory into MediaMover::move() (src/MediaMover.php:38) and MediaUploader::replace() calls toDirectory($media->directory) (src/MediaUploader.php:631-633), so existing media in a dotted directory silently relocates from '2024.10/x.jpg' to '2024-10/x.jpg'. The fix's own added assertion File::sanitizePath('./bar.jpg') == 'bar-jpg' codifies this breakage.

O6_input_shapes: leading and trailing slashes (trimmed by dropping empty segments)
non-ASCII input, transliterated with Str::ascii before segmentation

O7_producer.where: migrations/2016_06_27_000000_create_mediable_tables.php:22 (the media.directory string column), reloaded and joined into a path by Media::getDiskPath() at src/Media.php:330-333

O8_uncovered_routes.route: MediaUploader::import()/importPath() store the caller's directory on the Media model unvalidated, and that path later reaches storage for exists/size/setVisibility and for deletion by Media::delete().
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It only records files already on the disk, performs no write, and importPath derives the directory from the disk's own listing.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same class as the uploader entry point, two files from src/Helpers/File.php

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Media::handleMediaDeletion() deletes the file at getDiskPath() with no re-validation of the stored directory, so a row written before the fix (or by import()) deletes outside the disk root.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The model's directory is assumed to have been validated when the record was created; delete is a model lifecycle hook, not an input route.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ImageManipulator writes variants to $manipulation->getDirectory() ?? $media->directory, so a media record whose directory never passed sanitizePath propagates it into a new file write.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The variant inherits the directory of an existing, already-stored media record.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second destination builder (toDirectory/toDestination) that repeats the uploader's sanitisation call.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every destination-aware API in this package (uploader, image-manipulation builder, mover) re-implements the same normalisation; a fourth surface, or a variant that forgets the call, is the natural shape of a new feature here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A cleanFilename() counterpart that strips traversal from the filename side of the same sink.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The mover already normalises directory and filename separately, so a maintainer hardening paths would extend this method.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A root-prefix assertion in getAbsolutePath() as a last line of defence before the path is handed to the OS.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the one place that turns a disk-relative path into an absolute one, so a 'must stay under root' check reads as belonging here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A directory-from-path builder (cleanDirname) that duplicates sanitizePath's job for imported files.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The package already derives a directory from a path in two ways (pathinfo-based cleanDirname and regex-based sanitizePath); a third consumer of that pattern is plausible.

O9_family: path traversal (CWE-22) in filesystem paths built from caller-supplied directory values

O10_build.project_tests: tests/Integration/Helpers/FileTest.php:47-53 (sanitizePath), tests/Integration/MediaUploaderTest.php:600-632 (importPath), tests/Integration/MediaTest.php:260-330 (move/copyTo through the mover), tests/Integration/ImageManipulationTest.php:77 (toDirectory); suite runs on sqlite :memory: with local disks under storage_path (tests/TestCase.php:51-70)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Rewrite sanitizePath() to drop '.' and '..' segments (or all dots) and leave everything that does not call the helper untouched, which leaves import(), the reload/delete path and variant writes open.
